In general, Neighborhood #1 is a fairly stable area, drawing most of its popularity from its proximity to the CBD and its view of the Susquehanna River area.
Neighborhoods #2 and #3 are similar in physical character. The distinction that separates neighborhood #2 from #3 is that of age and character of the people who live in the areas. These neighborhoods are part of a large geographic area of the City known as the "uptown" area.
b. Neighborhood #2:
Neighborhood #2 developed from an older, upper-middle and middle income residential area. Over the years the area has been subject to a fair amount of instability and deterioration; however, many of the original residents have remained and there appears to be an above average concentration of older persons. The relatively high percentage of whites in the area may also be due in part to this older population. Elderly people also prefer this area because it is within an accessible distance to downtown shopping areas.
c. Neighborhood #3:
Neighborhood #3 is the "heart" neighborhood of the project. It contains the largest number of residential properties. It has the largest number of sub-standard properties (both flood damaged and generally deteriorated). It has the greatest social needs. This neighborhood is, in reality, a segment of a much larger general neighborhood area covering a large portion of the City's area to the east of the project. This larger neighborhood area includes most of the Hamilton NDP Area and a narrow strip of community not designated as a Federal project area. This strip lies between the project and the Hamilton NDP Project (see Project Location Map, appendix B). The relationship between this narrow strip of community and the project area will be discussed later in this report.
6. The Community as it Relates to the Project
The community that affects the project to the greatest degree is the City of Harrisburg proper. Other Townships within the metropolitan area and the Tri-county Regional Area surrounding Harrisburg exerts influence on the project, but to a lesser extent. Therefore, the following discussions of the general Harrisburg area and its various physical, social, cultural, and economic facets will help put the project itself into prospective.
